telemetry_sources: Packet capture at the WKS-4471 and WKS-4472 network interfaces
environment._constraint: This scenario has NO host telemetry. There are no process, file, registry or authentication events available — only network flows. Endpoint agent coverage does not extend to these hosts.

alert.rule_name: Workstation-to-Workstation DCERPC Session on a Service-Control Endpoint
alert.description: A workstation opened an RPC endpoint-mapper session to a peer workstation and immediately followed it with a session to the dynamic port returned by that mapper, uploading a payload substantially larger than the response. Workstation-to-workstation RPC on service-control interfaces is the wire signature of remote service creation, a common remote-execution mechanism. Peer workstations normally have no reason to administer one another.
alert.detection_logic: NetworkFlow WHERE destination_port = 135 AND source_ip IN workstation_subnet AND destination_ip IN workstation_subnet FOLLOWED WITHIN 5s BY NetworkFlow FROM same source_ip TO same destination_ip ON ephemeral_port WHERE bytes_to_server > 4096
alert.data_source: Network sensor (flow records) at the WKS-4471 and WKS-4472 interfaces

enrichment.rpc_mechanics: TCP/135 is the RPC endpoint mapper. A client asks it which dynamic port serves a given interface UUID and then connects to that port. The pair of flows to 135 and then to 49726, nine milliseconds apart between the same two hosts, is one logical RPC operation, not two unrelated connections.
enrichment.byte_asymmetry: As recorded at the WKS-4472 sensor, the flow to port 49726 carries 8,693 bytes toward the server against 1,454 bytes back. A service-control bind that only queried state would be small and roughly symmetric. An upload of that size on a service-control endpoint is consistent with a service being created and its payload or command line delivered.
enrichment.two_sided_capture: The 135 and 49726 flows appear at both sensors, which confirms the traffic actually reached WKS-4472 rather than being dropped in transit. Note the byte counts differ between the two views of the 49726 flow (1,296 vs 8,693 bytes to server) — the WKS-4471 sensor did not capture the full uploaded payload, so the target-side view is the accurate one.
enrichment.kerberos_flow: One second before the RPC, WKS-4471 opened a flow to DC01 on TCP/88 receiving 1,671 bytes with nothing sent at the application layer in this capture. Port 88 is Kerberos; a service-ticket request for a service principal on the target is what a client does immediately before authenticating to it.
enrichment.pre_existing_beacon: The flow from WKS-4471:56495 to 10.24.9.50:80 was already established before the lateral movement and carries 236 packets with a strongly asymmetric byte ratio (5,766 sent, 62,000 received). 10.24.9.50 is outside the internal address ranges used by the hosts in this capture.
enrichment.post_movement_beacon: The decisive record is the last flow: at 16:17:01.658, five seconds after the RPC session, WKS-4472 originates its own connection to the same external address and port, 10.24.9.50:80, with the same asymmetric profile. WKS-4472 had no prior contact with that address anywhere in the capture.
enrichment.interpretation_constraint: Only network flows are available. Which process opened these sockets, which account authenticated, and what the created service ran cannot be determined from this telemetry and must be listed as requiring endpoint verification.
